items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: Meade 'Lux' Lewis stayed there on one of his engagements in New York. He stayed at the house and the night that he got killed he had just left from The House That Jazz Built.

ctx.x: Yeah, well the House That Jazz Built was a little building that we bought in 1956. And when we first had it, well first of all, Orville, my son was going to music school and I set it up so he would have a little studio over there. And there was a space over there for some of the musicians that were in and out of town. That was a place for them to leave their

trunk, and they had sort of a little dorm over there. Vic And/Dickenson lived there. Marcus Foster, Ron Scott, Jimmy Rainey, and in fact the Meade "Lux" Lewis stayed there on one of his engagements in New York. He stayed at the house and the night that he got killed he had just left from The House That Jazz Built. So after the guys, most of them got settled with apartments of their own - and then of course, there was nobody living there. This was Cliff's baby, you know.
